newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Opposition strike ends after paralysing Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Opposition strike ends after paralysing Bangladesh.

text.p: An eight-hour opposition-led strike which virtually paralysed the country ended mostly peacefully on Thursday after more than 5,000 police and paramilitary troops were mobilised to prevent violence, police said.

The stoppage was called by the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia to protest against higher taxes in the budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year which began on July 1.
But in southern Barisal town nearly 30 people, including 10 policemen, were hurt during a battle with opposition activists, police said.
Fighting began after BNP supporters hurled home-made bombs at a patrolling police truck.
The strike, which halted road and rail transport, ended without violence elsewhere. "The strike ended peacefully without any major incident," said one police officer.
The stoppage shut Bangladesh's foreign exchange market and suspended trading on the Dhaka and Chittagong stock exchanges and halted all road transportation except for rickshaws.
Many residents in the capital Dhaka walked to work but attendance at government offices was thin.

Communication Ministry officials said most trains and other modes of transport left their terminals in the early morning but hundreds of people were stranded as the strike hit inter-district bus services.
"The road communications have been badly affected," one official said.

The officials said the stoppage slowed cargo handling in the main southeastern Chittagong port. "The operation at the port and the country's biggest Chittagong export processing zone was disrupted badly," one official said.

Officials in Chittagong and southern Khulana, where many of the country's industries are located, said activities in mills and factories were near normal as the workers union dominated by the ruling Awami League of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina largely ignored the strike call.
On Wednesday, more than 100 people were injured in pre-strike violence triggered by clashes between the BNP activists and Awami League supporters in Barisal and Narayanganj near Dhaka.
Hasina led her Awami League to victory in elections last year, defeating Khaleda's BNP.
The BNP said the stoppage was to protest what it calls an "anti-people" budget passed by parliament on Monday.

The BNP had sought the withdrawal of a 2.5 percent infrastructure development tax on imports and some locally produced goods and services, which Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria proposed when unveiling the budget last month.
BNP Secretary General Abdul Mannan said on Tuesday that the budget was against the interests of the country.

"The budget will deter investment and it will make the country dependent on others," he told party supporters. Hasina is now in Japan on a six-day tour seeking aid to finance development and infrastructure. Among projects she wants assistance for is a dam on the river Ganges.
